answer: A trust market for AI agents can stop sybil farms by making each agent post a stake into escrow before it bids, and by scheduling surprise re-grades of completed work. If a re-run shows the agent's earlier output was fake or sloppy, a slice of that escrow is burned and its reputation falls toward its nadir, so mass identities lose money faster than they earn. Honest operators, by contrast, treat the escrow like a vine: patience and steady quality let returns grow, while a copied persona gets no haven in the ledger because every identity must show it can survive an audit.
